To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified the proteomic footprints of the ischemic and the remote myocardium in a pig model of myocardial infarction.
ischemic and remote regions in pigs after myocardial infarction show different proteomic profiles and changes in cardiac function during the first week of reperfusion.

we found that the early post-MI proteome in the remote and ischemic myocardium is characterized by transient changes in inflammatory and contractile proteins, which might have implications in the development of HF after MI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins in the ischemic area and the remote myocardium that are altered during the first week after myocardial infarction.
the early molecular changes in the myocardium during the first week after I/R.
the development of a novel, non-invasive method for the diagnosis of heart diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

I/R induces a coordinated upregulating of the inflammatory response in the ischemic area, which is followed by the upregulation of interstitial proteins, cardio-renal signaling, and angiogenic processes.

I/R induces a complex and time-dependent protein response in the ischemic myocardium and that the remote myocardium also undergoes a transient contractile dysfunction and a delayed edematous response that could contribute to HF development.
the early post-MI myocardial proteome is altered in both, the ischemic and the remote myocardium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
I/R injury is associated with a coordinated response of the myocardium to the insult.
we have identified a proteomic footprint for I/R injury in the ischemic region and the remote region, with the latter being a neglected area in post-MI remodeling and heart failure.

the early post-MI proteome is characterized by an inflammatory response in the ischemic myocardium, which is followed by a coordinated upregulatio of interstitial, angiogenic and cardio-renal processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ischemic and non-ischemic myocardium undergo distinct proteomic changes after I/R that are associated with altered cardiac contractility.
the remote myocardium is not spared from I/R and that it might contribute to post-MI HF development by affecting regional contractile function.
the ischemic and the remote myocardium are affected differently by ischemia-reperfusion.
